findings: The action compiler reuses function-action capture and publishes sounds before classification, named broadcasts only when all broadcasts are parameter-free and compiled listeners exist, and one counter-named synthetic message for direct overlay/tracked effects. Duplicate broadcasts, persists flags, missing listeners, empty captures and side-effect-only handled results preserve the actual native pass.

The raw action reader retains the original outer table and all actor inputs throughout the pass and the current entry through its callback. It reads the next current raw slot after each callback instead of freezing entries or reloading a replacement global, bypasses table/entry metamethods and stops at the first nil slot.

Beat conversion follows existing read_f32: numeric values must remain finite as f32; valid UTF-8 strings use trimmed Rust parsing including the existing string NaN/infinity behavior; malformed beats skip entries; only nil/false suppress persists. Invalid UTF-8 named action strings are hard errors with prior publication preserved.

Failed or unhandled function captures increment the existing unsupported counter, deduplicate the existing beat/persists detail and continue later entries. Hard parser errors propagate. Native host functions and Lua closures are accepted. No Lua C API compatibility or generic mlua facade was added.
